title: Bangkok Dangerous
full_review:
In the grim shoot-‘em-up “Bangkok Dangerous” (Lionsgate), Joe (Nicholas Cage), a solitary hit man, travels to the titular city to carry out four contract killings for a local crime boss (Nirattisai Kaljareuk). This, he hopes, will be the lucrative climax of his career.

Once there, however, he falls under the exotic city’s spell and finds the emotional isolation necessary to his work thawed by his friendship for Kong (Shahkrit Yamnarm), the petty thief he hires as an assistant, and by his feelings for the pretty Fon (Charlie Young), a pharmacy clerk who can neither hear nor speak.

As directed by the Pang Brothers, this remake of their 1999 Thai film features considerable violence and muddled moral values, with its hero instructing his protege in the art of killing even while ostensibly reassessing his own viciousness.

The film contains brief graphic sexual activity, upper female nudity, intense action violence with gore, suicide and occasional rough and crude language. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is L -- limited adult audience, films whose problematic content many adults would find troubling. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
